exposure: COVID-19 infection (including timing of infection in trimester, presence of symptoms, hospitalization, ICU admission)
outcome: mental health (measured by Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale - EPDS scores)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 530 pregnant women with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 infection who agreed to participate.
finding: More than half of the pregnant women infected with COVID-19 experienced anxiety and fear, with a 67% prevalence of depression and anxiety, which was significantly associated with the severity of COVID-19 infection (symptoms, hospitalization, ICU admission), smoking status, and method of delivery.
mod_finding: EPDS scores were statistically significantly associated with the method of delivery.
